title: Why procrastination is not about willpower

creativeDirection.performance: direct-to-camera with natural pauses and calm emphasis
creativeDirection.visualContinuity: preserve the original founder, clothing, hair, lighting, plants, bench, and laptop throughout
creativeDirection.captionStyle: clean high-contrast two-line captions in the lower safe area

scenes.dialogue: If procrastination were really about will power, why do we avoid the tasks that matter most?
scenes.visual: Founder full-screen, direct eye contact, gentle 2 percent push-in.
scenes.retentionBeat: Emphasize WILLPOWER and MATTER MOST in captions.

scenes.dialogue: Psychologically, procrastination is often emotional avoidance.
scenes.visual: Hold on founder; no cut so the insight feels personal and credible.
scenes.retentionBeat: Caption emphasis shifts from WILLPOWER to EMOTIONAL AVOIDANCE.

scenes.dialogue: A task can trigger fear of failure, perfectionism, uncertainty, or overwhelm. Avoiding it gives your brain immediate relief, so the habit gets stronger.
scenes.visual: Founder remains full-screen; subtle crop change at 14 seconds creates a pattern interrupt.
scenes.retentionBeat: Reveal FEAR, PERFECTIONISM, UNCERTAINTY, and OVERWHELM one phrase at a time.

scenes.dialogue: Instead of asking, "Why am I so lazy?" ask, "What feeling am I avoiding?"
scenes.visual: Return to the original crop and let the founder's expression carry the beat.
scenes.retentionBeat: Use the two questions as consecutive caption cards.

scenes.dialogue: Then make the next step smaller: open the document, write one line, or work for just two minutes.
scenes.visual: Gentle push-in; hold the final frame for recognition.
